title: Claude Code Plugins
one_liner: A plugin packages skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers as one installable unit, usually distributed through a marketplace.

core.title: A plugin is a directory of components with a manifest
core.body: Components can be skills, agents, hooks, a hooks module, and MCP servers. The manifest at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` supplies the name and optional version and description.
core.why: The unit of install, update and removal is the plugin, not the individual component.

quotes.text: A Claude Code plugin is a directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or other components that Claude Code installs and loads as one unit.
quotes.label: Plugins overview

quotes.text: The manifest, a JSON file at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, gives the plugin its name
quotes.label: Plugins > What a plugin is

diagram.caption: Plugin layout shown in the docs diagram

core.title: Use a plugin to package and share, not to enable
core.body: Skills, subagents, hooks and MCP servers all work without a plugin. Make or install a plugin to move several of them together, share with teammates, or publish versioned releases.
core.why: Wrapping a single personal skill in a plugin adds overhead without benefit.

quotes.text: Skills, subagents, hooks, and MCP servers all work on their own, without a plugin.
quotes.label: Plugins > Decide whether you need a plugin

quotes.text: Use a plugin when you want several skills, subagents, hooks, or MCP servers packaged as one unit.
quotes.label: Plugins > Decide whether you need a plugin

core.title: A marketplace is a catalog, not a store
core.body: A marketplace is a repository or directory with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. You add it once, then install plugins by name, for example `commit-commands@claude-plugins-official`.
core.why: Adding a marketplace does not install anything; installing a plugin does.

quotes.text: A marketplace is a repository or directory with a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` file that lists plugins and where to fetch each one.
quotes.label: Plugins > Get plugins from a marketplace

quotes.text: It's a catalog, not a hosted store.
quotes.label: Plugins > Get plugins from a marketplace

core.title: Install scope decides who gets the plugin
core.body: User scope: you, all projects. Project scope: everyone in the repository through the committed `.claude/settings.json`, though each person still installs it. Local scope: you, this repository only.
core.why: Project scope shares the setting, not the files. Collaborators still need to install.

quotes.text: User scope: enabled for you in every project on this computer
quotes.label: Plugins > Install scopes

quotes.text: Local scope: enabled for you in this repository only
quotes.label: Plugins > Install scopes

core.title: An enabled plugin costs context in every session
core.body: Names and descriptions of invocable skills, agents and commands are in context on every turn. MCP servers run alongside each session and hooks fire at their events. Disable a plugin with `/plugin` or `claude plugin disable` without uninstalling.
core.why: Unused plugins still consume tokens and leave less room in the context window.

quotes.text: An enabled plugin is part of every session, not only the sessions where you use it.
quotes.label: Plugins > What an enabled plugin adds

quotes.text: The full text of a skill or agent loads only when it's used.
quotes.label: Plugins > What an enabled plugin adds

core.title: A plugin runs with your privileges
core.body: Anthropic's official, community and third-party marketplaces differ by name tier, but any plugin can run code as you. Review a plugin before installing it.
core.why: Official status does not remove the need to review what a plugin runs.

quotes.text: a plugin you install can run code with your user privileges.
quotes.label: Plugins > Marketplace tiers

practice.title: Inspect your plugin setup
practice.goal: See the marketplace-to-session path on your machine.
steps: Run `/plugin` in a Claude Code terminal session
Open the **Discover** tab and pick a plugin from the official marketplace
Open the plugin from the **Marketplaces** tab and read its **Context cost** estimate
practice.check: You can name the marketplace, the plugin, and its estimated context cost.
practice.variation: Compare a plugin with several components against one with a single skill.

practice.title: Disable without uninstalling
steps: Check the **Installed** tab for the **Not used recently** group
Disable one plugin with `claude plugin disable` in your shell, or in `/plugin`
practice.check: The plugin's skills no longer appear, and the plugin is still listed as installed.

gotchas: A plugin marketplace is not Claude Marketplace, the website at claude.com/marketplace. You cannot add the website with `/plugin marketplace add`.
Project-scope plugins are enabled in committed settings, but each collaborator must still install them on their own machine.
Cloud sessions, including claude.ai/code, do not load the plugins in your local settings.
The VS Code extension and the JetBrains plugin are not Claude Code plugins.

recall.a: A directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers or other components installed and loaded as one unit.

recall.q: When do you not need a plugin?
recall.a: When a skill, subagent, hook or MCP server on its own is enough.

recall.q: Does adding a marketplace install its plugins?
recall.a: No. A marketplace is a catalog; you install plugins from it by name.
The enabled setting through committed `.claude/settings.json`. Each collaborator still installs the plugin.

recall.q: Why can an installed but unused plugin still matter?
recall.a: Its descriptions are in context every turn, and its MCP servers and hooks run in each session.
